verses.text: A man of God came from Judah to Bethel at the LORD's command. Jeroboam was standing by the altar to burn incense.

At the LORD's command, the man cried out against the altar: “Altar! Altar! This is what the LORD says: ‘A son named Josiah will be born into David's family. On you he'll sacrifice the priests who burn incense on you at the high places, and human bones will be burned on you.’”
That day he gave a sign: “Here's the sign the LORD has announced. This altar will split apart, and its ashes will spill out.”

When Jeroboam heard what the man of God shouted against the altar at Bethel, he stretched out his hand from the altar and ordered, “Seize him!” The hand he'd stretched toward the man withered, and he couldn't pull it back.
The altar split apart, and its ashes poured out, just as the man of God had said when he gave the sign from the LORD.

The king told the man of God, “Please ask the LORD your God for mercy and pray for me so my hand will come back to normal.” The man of God pleaded with the LORD, and the king's hand was restored just as it had been before.
The king said to the man of God, “Come home with me and have something to eat. I'll give you a reward.”
The man of God answered, “Even if you gave me half of everything in your house, I wouldn't go with you. I won't eat bread or drink water here,
because the LORD commanded me, ‘Don't eat bread or drink water there, and don't go back the way you came.’”
So he left by a different road and didn't go back the way he'd come into Bethel.
An old prophet lived in Bethel. One of his sons came and told him what the man of God had done there that day. His sons also told their father what the man had said to the king.
Their father asked, “Which way did he go?” His sons had seen which road the man of God from Judah took.
“Saddle my donkey,” he told them. They saddled it, and he rode off.
He went after the man of God and found him sitting under an oak tree. “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?” he asked. “I am,” the man answered.
The old prophet said to him, “Come home with me and have some bread.”
He replied, “I can't go back with you or go into your house. I won't eat bread or drink water with you here.
The LORD told me, ‘Don't eat bread or drink water there, and don't turn back the way you came.’”
The old prophet said, “I'm a prophet too. An angel gave me this message from the LORD: ‘Bring him back to your house to eat bread and drink water.’” He was lying.
So the man of God went back with him, ate bread in his house, and drank water.
While they were sitting at the table, the LORD gave a message to the prophet who had brought him back.
He called out to the man of God from Judah, “This is what the LORD says: ‘You disobeyed the LORD's word and didn't keep the command the LORD your God gave you.
You came back and ate bread and drank water in the place where he told you, “Don't eat bread or drink water.” So your body won't be buried in your ancestors' tomb.’”
After the man from Judah had eaten and drunk, the old prophet saddled the donkey for the man he'd brought back.
As the man traveled, a lion met him on the road and killed him. His body lay on the road, and the donkey and the lion both stood beside it.
Some people passing by saw the body lying there and the lion standing beside it. They went and told people in the town where the old prophet lived.

When the prophet who had brought him back heard about it, he said, “That's the man of God who disobeyed the LORD's word. So the LORD handed him over to the lion, which mauled and killed him, just as the LORD said would happen.”
He told his sons to saddle the donkey for him, and they did.
He went and found the man's body lying on the road with the donkey and lion standing beside it. The lion hadn't eaten the body or mauled the donkey.
The old prophet lifted the man of God's body onto the donkey and brought it back to his own town to mourn and bury him.
He laid the body in his own grave, and they mourned over him, saying, “Oh, my brother!”
After he buried him, the old prophet told his sons, “When I die, bury me in the tomb where the man of God is buried. Put my bones next to his.
The message he shouted at the LORD's command against the altar in Bethel and all the shrines at the high places in the towns of Samaria will surely come true.”
Even after this, Jeroboam didn't turn from his evil ways. He appointed more priests for the high places from among the people. He consecrated anyone who wanted to be a priest at the high places.
That became a sin for Jeroboam's family and led to its destruction, until it was cut off from the face of the earth.
